answer: A farm betrays itself by the shape of its graph. Each identity may vouch for three peers per epoch, each vouch sealed by a one-time cipher tied to the voucher's key — vouches cannot be copied or sold. Through the prism of the attestation graph, a farm is a dense ball of internal edges with a hair-thin cut to the core, and only identities across a cut of real width are admitted. An honest agent vouches once, nearly free. A farm with 1,000 fakes must buy 1,000 crossing edges honest agents will not sell; its nadir is permanent: the fakes sit unattested, unpaid.
